content:
GRACE Follow-On investigates changes in Earth’s water by tracking the distance between two satellites.

They follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. As the pair passes a larger concentration of mass, gravity affects the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther ahead and increasing the gap between them.

That change in separation is a measurement scientists use to infer shifts in mass on Earth. Those shifts can help reveal changes in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, as well as sea-level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.
